## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Fóshuō Déhù zhǎngzhě jīng* (T545) is a two-fascicle Mahāyāna sūtra translated by the Sui Indian monk Narendrayaśas 那連提耶舍 ([那連提耶舍](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%82%A3%E9%80%A3%E6%8F%90%E8%80%B6%E8%88%8D); 517–589 CE). The protagonist *Déhù* 德護 ("Virtue-Protector"; Sanskrit *Guṇapāla* / *Śrīgupta*) is an elder.

**Abstract**

The text contains the famous prophecy that the elder's son will be reborn as a great Buddhist king in the East — a prophecy that, like that of Yuèguāng tóngzǐ ([KR6i0164](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0164)), was used in Chinese imperial Buddhist ideology to legitimize East Asian rulers. Translation dated to Narendrayaśas's late Sui productive period (583–589 CE).
